Plot a Cross-Validated Super Learner

Source: R/cv_super_learner.R
cv_sl_methods.Rd

Three plot types are provided:

type = "comparison" (default)

A fair comparison of the candidate learners against the super learner ensemble. For each learner — candidates and super_learner alike — bars and filled points show the mean held-out loss across the outer cross-validation folds, open circles show each outer fold's held-out loss, and ranges show \(\pm 1\) standard deviation across folds. Learners are ordered best (lowest mean loss) at top. This automates the figure shown in the package README.

type = "weights"

Ensemble-weight stability across the outer folds; delegated to plot.nadir_crossfit_sl(x$crossfit, type = "weights").

type = "fitted"

Out-of-fold ensemble predictions against observed outcomes; delegated to plot.nadir_crossfit_sl(x$crossfit, type = "fitted"). Not defined for outcome_type = "density" or "multiclass".

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nadir_cv_sl'
plot(x, type = c("comparison", "weights", "fitted"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nadir_cv_sl'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class nadir_cv_sl as returned by cv_super_learner().

type

One of "comparison", "weights", or "fitted".

...

Ignored; included for compatibility with the generic.

Value

A ggplot object, which prints when returned to the console.

Details

Why is this the fair comparison, rather than plot(super_learner(...))? A super_learner() fit's ensemble weights are chosen using its candidates' holdout predictions, so scoring the ensemble on those same holdouts is optimistically biased — which is why plot.nadir_sl_model deliberately omits the ensemble from its comparison. cv_super_learner() adds the outer layer of cross-validation needed to score the ensemble honestly, and this plot method scores every candidate on those same outer validation folds: within each outer fold, the candidate fits and the ensemble weights were all estimated entirely without the validation data they are evaluated on, and every learner is trained on the same outer training data. All quantities are derived from the fitted object (the per-fold super_learner() fits stored in $crossfit); nothing is re-fit, though each candidate is re-predicted once per outer fold.

The loss is the loss_metric stored at fit time (by default, mean squared error for continuous outcomes and negative log loss otherwise). Learners that errored on an outer training fold contribute no loss for that fold.

Requires the ggplot2 package (listed in Suggests).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cv_sl <- cv_super_learner(
    data = mtcars,
    formula = mpg ~ cyl + hp,
    n_folds = 3, inner_n_folds = 2,
    learners = list(mean = lnr_mean, lm = lnr_lm)
  )
  plot(cv_sl) # fair candidates-vs-ensemble comparison
  plot(cv_sl, type = "weights") # weight stability across outer folds
  plot(cv_sl, type = "fitted") # out-of-fold predictions vs. observed
}
#> The loss_metric is being inferred based on the outcome_type=continuous -> using CV-MSE
